reason: E1 directly states that RTA on Si/SiO2 induces high-anisotropy phases via substrate strain and demonstrates a ~40-fold coercivity increase in FeCoNiMnCu, supporting the core premises. However, the hypothesis proposes an L10-like phase in a FeCoNi-based alloy without Pt, whereas E1 achieves L10 ordering only with 50 at.% Pt addition; the claim that RTA alone induces L10 ordering in a Pt-free FeCoNi-based HEA is an overstatement not directly supported by the cited evidence. E2 provides background on magnetization but does not address ordering or coercivity mechanisms.
premises: RTA of transition metal alloy films on Si/SiO2 induces high-anisotropy phase formation via substrate-induced strain
RTA can produce L10-like chemically ordered phases in FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys
L10 ordering reduces lattice symmetry and enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy leads to significantly higher coercivity
The effect is specific to thin films where substrate-induced strain is effective
